lines.raw: In the US: The US approach.

lines.raw: Congress passes a **law** (an Act) that sets the goal.
lines.say: Congress passes a law (an Act) that sets the goal.

lines.raw: A federal agency writes detailed **rules** (called regulations or "final rules") that say exactly who must do what, and by when.
lines.say: A federal agency writes detailed rules (called regulations or "final rules") that say exactly who must do what, and by when.

lines.raw: The rules point to **standards** (formats and code sets) that everyone must use.
lines.say: The rules point to standards (formats and code sets) that everyone must use.

lines.raw: Those who break the rules can face penalties or lose payments.
lines.say: Those who break the rules can face penalties or lose payments.

lines.raw: The timeline.
lines.say: The timeline.

lines.raw: Key US laws and steps for health data sharing (simplified).
lines.say: Key U S laws and steps for health data sharing (simplified).

lines.raw: **1996**. Law or step: HIPAA. What it did for data sharing: Told the government to adopt national standards for electronic insurance transactions (claims, payments, eligibility checks) and code sets. Also led to the privacy and security rules.
lines.say: 1996. Law or step: HIPAA. What it did for data sharing: Told the government to adopt national standards for electronic insurance transactions (claims, payments, eligibility checks) and code sets. Also led to the privacy and security rules.

lines.raw: Early 2000s. Law or step: HIPAA transaction standards take effect. What it did for data sharing: Payers and providers had to exchange claims and related data in the standard **X12** and **NCPDP** formats.
lines.say: Early 2000s. Law or step: HIPAA transaction standards take effect. What it did for data sharing: Payers and providers had to exchange claims and related data in the standard X12 and N C P D P formats.

lines.raw: **2004**. Law or step: ONC created. What it did for data sharing: The Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT was set up to lead national health IT efforts.
lines.say: 2004. Law or step: O N C created. What it did for data sharing: The Office of the National Coordinator for Health I T was set up to lead national health I T efforts.

lines.raw: **2009**. Law or step: HITECH Act. What it did for data sharing: Paid hospitals and doctors incentives to adopt and meaningfully use **certified EHRs**. EHR use grew from a minority of hospitals to nearly all of them.
lines.say: 2009. Law or step: HITECH Act. What it did for data sharing: Paid hospitals and doctors incentives to adopt and meaningfully use certified E H R's. E H R use grew from a minority of hospitals to nearly all of them.

lines.raw: **2016**. Law or step: 21st Century Cures Act. What it did for data sharing: Banned **information blocking**, called for API access to health data "without special effort", and asked for a national framework to connect networks (lesson 7).
lines.say: 2016. Law or step: 21st Century Cures Act. What it did for data sharing: Banned information blocking, called for A P I access to health data "without special effort", and asked for a national framework to connect networks (lesson 7).

lines.raw: **2020**. Law or step: Cures Act rules from ONC and CMS. What it did for data sharing: ONC wrote the information blocking and certification details. CMS wrote rules requiring health plans to offer data through APIs (lesson 3).
lines.say: 2020. Law or step: Cures Act rules from O N C and C M S. What it did for data sharing: O N C wrote the information blocking and certification details. C M S wrote rules requiring health plans to offer data through A P I's (lesson 3).

lines.raw: **2024**. Law or step: More CMS rules, and ONC renamed. What it did for data sharing: CMS added prior authorisation and more API rules. ONC became part of a renamed office, **ASTP/ONC**.
lines.say: 2024. Law or step: More C M S rules, and O N C renamed. What it did for data sharing: C M S added prior authorisation and more A P I rules. O N C became part of a renamed office, ASTP/ONC.

lines.raw: Step 1: HIPAA, the first push.
lines.say: Step 1: HIPAA, the first push.

lines.raw: Before HIPAA, each insurer could ask for claims in its own layout.
lines.say: Before HIPAA, each insurer could ask for claims in its own layout.

lines.raw: A doctor's office dealing with dozens of insurers had to handle dozens of formats.
lines.say: A doctor's office dealing with dozens of insurers had to handle dozens of formats.

lines.raw: HIPAA's **Administrative Simplification** part said: everyone uses the **same electronic transactions** and the **same code sets**.
lines.say: HIPAA's Administrative Simplification part said: everyone uses the same electronic transactions and the same code sets.

lines.raw: That is why a claim today travels as an **X12 837** file coded with **ICD-10** and **CPT**, whichever insurer receives it.
lines.say: That is why a claim today travels as an X12 8 37 file coded with I C D 10 and C P T, whichever insurer receives it.

lines.raw: HIPAA does two jobs.
lines.say: HIPAA does two jobs.

lines.raw: Most people know HIPAA for **privacy**.
lines.say: Most people know HIPAA for privacy.

lines.raw: For data people, its standard transactions matter just as much.
lines.say: For data people, its standard transactions matter just as much.

lines.raw: The HIPAA course covers both in detail.
lines.say: The HIPAA course covers both in detail.

lines.raw: Step 2: HITECH and the move to EHRs.
lines.say: Step 2: HITECH and the move to E H R's.

scenes.section: Step 2: HITECH and the move to EHRs

lines.raw: HIPAA standardised the **insurance** side, but clinical records were still mostly on paper.
lines.say: HIPAA standardised the insurance side, but clinical records were still mostly on paper.

lines.raw: The **HITECH Act** of 2009 changed that with money.
lines.say: The HITECH Act of 2009 changed that with money.

lines.raw: Hospitals and doctors who adopted **certified** EHR software and used it in set ways ("meaningful use") received incentive payments from Medicare and Medicaid.
lines.say: Hospitals and doctors who adopted certified E H R software and used it in set ways ("meaningful use") received incentive payments from Medicare and Medicaid.

lines.raw: Later, Medicare turned this into payment **reductions** for those who did not take part.
lines.say: Later, Medicare turned this into payment reductions for those who did not take part.

lines.raw: The program is now called **Promoting Interoperability**.
lines.say: The program is now called Promoting Interoperability.

scenes.section: Step 2: HITECH and the move to EHRs

lines.raw: Digital is not the same as connected.
lines.say: Digital is not the same as connected.

lines.raw: By the late 2010s most US hospitals had EHRs.
lines.say: By the late 2010s most U S hospitals had E H R's.

lines.raw: But many EHRs still could not talk to each other easily.
lines.say: But many E H R's still could not talk to each other easily.

lines.raw: Getting records **digital** came first.
lines.say: Getting records digital came first.

lines.raw: Getting them **connected** needed the next law.
lines.say: Getting them connected needed the next law.

lines.raw: Step 3: the 21st Century Cures Act.
lines.say: Step 3: the 21st Century Cures Act.

lines.raw: Passed in **December 2016**, the Cures Act covered many topics.
lines.say: Passed in December 2016, the Cures Act covered many topics.

lines.raw: For data, its big idea was **information blocking**: practices that unreasonably stop electronic health information from being accessed, exchanged or used.
lines.say: For data, its big idea was information blocking: practices that unreasonably stop electronic health information from being accessed, exchanged or used.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Healthcare providers (hospitals, doctors). Example of blocking: Refusing to send results to a competing clinic the patient chose. Allowed reasons not to share (simplified): Protecting privacy, keeping systems secure, preventing harm.
lines.say: Healthcare providers (hospitals, doctors). Example of blocking: Refusing to send results to a competing clinic the patient chose. Allowed reasons not to share (simplified): Protecting privacy, keeping systems secure, preventing harm.

lines.raw: Health IT developers (EHR makers). Example of blocking: Charging unreasonable fees to connect another system. Allowed reasons not to share (simplified): The request is truly not feasible.
lines.say: Health I T developers (E H R makers). Example of blocking: Charging unreasonable fees to connect another system. Allowed reasons not to share (simplified): The request is truly not feasible.

lines.raw: Health information exchanges and networks. Example of blocking: Only sharing with members who buy extra services. Allowed reasons not to share (simplified): Reasonable, fair fees and licences are allowed.
lines.say: Health information exchanges and networks. Example of blocking: Only sharing with members who buy extra services. Allowed reasons not to share (simplified): Reasonable, fair fees and licences are allowed.

lines.raw: The detailed rules list specific **exceptions**, so not every refusal is blocking.
lines.say: The detailed rules list specific exceptions, so not every refusal is blocking.

lines.raw: Penalties differ by type of actor and are still being phased in, so phrase them carefully at work: "information blocking can lead to penalties or payment disincentives".
lines.say: Penalties differ by type of actor and are still being phased in, so phrase them carefully at work: "information blocking can lead to penalties or payment disincentives".

lines.say: O N C, certified health I T and U S C D I.

scenes.section: ONC, certified health IT and USCDI

lines.raw: ONC (now ASTP/ONC).
lines.say: O N C (now ASTP/ONC).

lines.raw: The federal office that leads US health IT policy.
lines.say: The federal office that leads U S health I T policy.

lines.raw: In **2024** it was reorganised and renamed, and it is now usually written **ASTP/ONC** (Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy / Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT).
lines.say: In 2024 it was reorganised and renamed, and it is now usually written ASTP/ONC (Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy or Office of the National Coordinator for Health I T).

lines.raw: Many people still just say "ONC".
lines.say: Many people still just say "O N C".

lines.raw: Certified health IT.
lines.say: Certified health I T.

lines.raw: EHR software that has passed ONC's certification program, proving it can do required things, such as export records in standard formats and offer a standard FHIR API.
lines.say: E H R software that has passed ONC's certification program, proving it can do required things, such as export records in standard formats and offer a standard F H I R A P I.

lines.raw: Medicare programs expect providers to use certified software.
lines.say: Medicare programs expect providers to use certified software.

lines.raw: USCDI.
lines.say: U S C D I.

lines.raw: The **United States Core Data for Interoperability**: an agreed list of data elements that certified systems must be able to share.
lines.say: The United States Core Data for Interoperability: an agreed list of data elements that certified systems must be able to share.

lines.raw: It grows in new versions over time.
lines.say: It grows in new versions over time.

scenes.section: ONC, certified health IT and USCDI

lines.raw: Some USCDI data classes, with Robert as the example.
lines.say: Some U S C D I data classes, with Robert as the example.

lines.raw: Patient demographics. What it includes: Name, date of birth, sex, address, phone. Robert example: Robert Carter, born 2 May 1957, Houston TX.
lines.say: Patient demographics. What it includes: Name, date of birth, sex, address, phone. Robert example: Robert Carter, born 2 May 1957, Houston T X.

lines.raw: Problems. What it includes: Conditions the patient has. Robert example: Type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure.
lines.say: Problems. What it includes: Conditions the patient has. Robert example: Type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure.

lines.raw: Medications. What it includes: Medicines the patient takes. Robert example: Metformin, lisinopril.
lines.say: Medications. What it includes: Medicines the patient takes. Robert example: Metformin, lisinopril.

lines.raw: Laboratory. What it includes: Tests and results. Robert example: HbA1c 9.4%.
lines.say: Laboratory. What it includes: Tests and results. Robert example: H b A 1 c 9.4 percent.

lines.raw: Vital signs. What it includes: Blood pressure, weight, height. Robert example: Blood pressure 148/92.
lines.say: Vital signs. What it includes: Blood pressure, weight, height. Robert example: Blood pressure 148/92.

lines.raw: Allergies and intolerances. What it includes: Substances that cause reactions. Robert example: None known.
lines.say: Allergies and intolerances. What it includes: Substances that cause reactions. Robert example: None known.

lines.raw: Health insurance information. What it includes: Coverage details (added in a later version). Robert example: His Medicare health plan member ID.
lines.say: Health insurance information. What it includes: Coverage details (added in a later version). Robert example: His Medicare health plan member I D.

lines.raw: Why USCDI matters to an analyst.
lines.say: Why U S C D I matters to an analyst.

lines.raw: USCDI is the "minimum common menu".
lines.say: U S C D I is the "minimum common menu".

lines.raw: If you receive clinical data from many different EHRs, the USCDI items are the ones you can most reasonably expect to find, in a standard form.
lines.say: If you receive clinical data from many different E H R's, the U S C D I items are the ones you can most reasonably expect to find, in a standard form.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **HIPAA (1996)** created standard electronic insurance transactions and code sets: the first big push.
lines.say: HIPAA (1996) created standard electronic insurance transactions and code sets: the first big push.

lines.raw: **HITECH (2009)** paid providers to adopt **certified EHRs**, so most clinical records became digital.
lines.say: HITECH (2009) paid providers to adopt certified E H R's, so most clinical records became digital.

lines.raw: The **21st Century Cures Act (2016)** banned **information blocking** and pushed standard APIs.
lines.say: The 21st Century Cures Act (2016) banned information blocking and pushed standard A P I's.

lines.raw: **ONC** (renamed **ASTP/ONC** in 2024) certifies health IT; **USCDI** is the common set of data elements.
lines.say: O N C (renamed ASTP/ONC in 2024) certifies health I T; U S C D I is the common set of data elements.
